land.text: Kebbi: Leka, Surame and Birnin Kebbi in the Rima and Zamfara valleys (the page gives no outline)

predecessors.note: Kanta Kuta, ruler of Leka, revolted against the dendi fari ("the governor") of Songhai in 1516-7 after a dispute over the booty of an expedition against Air; Songhai failed to restore control in 1517-18.

land.text: Kebbi: Leka, Surame and Birnin Kebbi in the Rima and Zamfara valleys (the page gives no outline)

successors.note: Abdullahi dan Fodio defeated Kebbi in 1808, took Birnin Kebbi and founded the Gwandu Emirate; Kebbi continued under Muhammadu Hodi in the Zamfara valley and Karari at Argungu (the Argungu Kebbi Emirate from 1831/1849, independence recognised in 1867).

capitals.name: Surame
capitals.note: "Surame was the capital of the kingdom" in the 16th century; the infobox also lists Birnin Leka; coordinates are approximate and not on the page.

capitals.name: Birnin Kebbi
capitals.note: Kanta fortified Birnin Kebbi as "his base in defence against the Songhay"; the page does not date a move of the capital (1600 is a bridge); Abdullahi took Birnin Kebbi in 1808.

correction.text: Kebbi: Leka, Surame and Birnin Kebbi in the Rima and Zamfara valleys (the page gives no outline)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kebbi row). Kanta Kuta of Leka revolted in 1516-7; the page gives no area ("a small but formidable empire" under Kanta, declining by the mid-17th century). The Kebbi State stands for the core; the imperial reach (Hausaland tributes, Yauri, Nupe, Agadez) is carried by vassal events, not in the shape.

keyframe_review.note: The Fulani conquest is dated 1808 by this page (1805 in the Sokoto dossier); Birnin Kebbi taken and Gwandu founded, Kebbi never fully conquered.

region.text: Kebbi: Leka, Surame and Birnin Kebbi in the Rima and Zamfara valleys (the page gives no outline)

ledger.note: 1516-7: Kanta Kuta revolts and Kebbi breaks from Songhai. "In the year 1516-7 Kanta Kuta, ruler of Leka, revolted against the dendi fari"; the revolt followed a dispute over the governor's refusal to share booty from an expedition against the Sultanate of Air.

Kebbi: Leka, Surame and Birnin Kebbi in the Rima and Zamfara valleys, the heartland of the kingdom, which the keyframe holds directly

region.text: the tributary lands of Hausaland, without Kebbi's own heartland (Kebbi State), which the keyframe holds as direct land

ledger.note: under Muhammad Kanta (took power probably 1523-24): Kebbi "had conquered vast territories and exacted tributes from much of Hausaland". The page gives no year; 1525 is a bridge. It also "expanded into Yauri and Nupe". [fx-39, R068: the region no longer includes Kebbi's own heartland (Kebbi State): the tribute relation drew those cells in the vassal tint, and the end of the tribute in 1650 released them to nobody, so the kingdom had no land from 1650 to 1808.]

region.text: Agadez, which Kebbi occupied 'capturing the region from Songhay'

ledger.note: under Kanta: Kebbi occupies Agadez. "Kebbi occupied Agadez, capturing the region from Songhay"; the page gives no year (1530 is a bridge). The songhai-empire dossier has Songhai taking Aïr in 1515.

region.text: Agadez, which Kebbi occupied 'capturing the region from Songhay'

ledger.note: late 16th century: Agadez breaks away. "In the late 16th century after Kanta's death, Agadez broke away from Kebbi"; the Kebbi page: Kano and Katsina "intervened in support of a claimant" and "Kebbi lost control of Agadez". 1580 is a bridging year.

Kebbi: Leka, Surame and Birnin Kebbi in the Rima and Zamfara valleys, the heartland of the kingdom, which the keyframe holds directly

region.text: the tributary lands of Hausaland, without Kebbi's own heartland (Kebbi State), which the keyframe holds as direct land

ledger.note: by the mid-17th century: the Kebbi empire declines. "Declined by the mid-17th century"; Zamfara "successfully revolted and secured their full independence" in the early 18th century. Bridge for the end of the Hausa tributes. [fx-39, R068: closing the relation (the compiler closes the whole vassal relation, whatever the region) now releases only the tributary lands of Hausaland, e.g. the Zinder country, and not the heartland, which stays Kebbi's direct land under the keyframe until 1808. The Kebbi page dates the end of tribute to Kanta's death: 'in 1556 Kanta died, and the Hausa states stopped paying tribute'; it also has Kebbi 'one of the leading states in Hausaland at the turn of the 19th century' and its tributaries Gobir and Zamfara revolt only 'by the early 18th century'. 1650 is kept as the bridge between those sentences.]

ledger.note: 1808: the Fulani take Birnin Kebbi. "In that year, Abdullahi dan Fodio defeated the forces of Kebbi"; he "took Birnin Kebbi and founded the Gwandu Emirate, but he never fully conquered Kebbi". The Sokoto dossier dates the gain to 1805.

ledger.note: 1808: the Kingdom of Kebbi ends as a Hausa power; Muhammadu Hodi resists in the Zamfara valley and Karari at Argungu (survivors, later the Kebbi Emirate of Argungu).

wars.name: Songhai-Kebbi wars

zones.text: Agadez, which Kebbi occupied 'capturing the region from Songhay'

wars.outcome: Songhai tried to restore control in 1517-18 and failed; Kanta routed the armies of Askia Muhammad Bunkan ("a crushing defeat") and no later Askia attacked Kebbi again.

wars.name: Kebbi-Bornu war
wars.outcome: "Bornu invaded Hausa states under Kanta's control, however he routed their armies."

wars.name: Fulani conquest of Kebbi

zones.text: Kebbi: Leka, Surame and Birnin Kebbi in the Rima and Zamfara valleys (the page gives no outline)

wars.outcome: Abdullahi dan Fodio defeated Kebbi in 1808 and founded Gwandu; Muhammadu Hodi and Karari resisted; after Karari died in 1831 his son Yakubu Nabame surrendered; Argungu was recognised as independent in 1867.

certainty.note: No frontier on the page; the imperial reach under Kanta was tribute, not annexation.

sources.title: Sultanate of Agadez
sources.note: Agadez broke away from Kebbi in the late 16th century after Kanta's death.

sources.title: Kebbi Kingdom
sources.note: Identity, 1516-7 revolt from Songhai, Kanta's conquests (undated), Agadez, Zamfara revolt, Fulani conquest 1808, Argungu survival; no area.

notes:
Kingdom of Kebbi (Hausa/Kebbawa kingdom of Kanta), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Page: Kebbi Kingdom (1 page).

The three imperial events (tribute from Hausaland 1525, Agadez 1530, loss of Agadez 1580 (Agadez page), end of tribute 1650) are bridges at confidence 1: the page names Kanta's conquests without years. Dates conflict: Fulani conquest 1808 (this page) versus 1805 (Sokoto dossier); the infobox shows unlabelled spans 1516-1561 and 1826-1827; the Songhai dossier has the Askia taking Air in 1515, before Kebbi's revolt. The Argungu continuation (Kebbi Emirate, independence recognised by treaty in 1867, Sama'ila's wars against Gwandu 1883-1903, British protectorate undated) is not covered here: a later dossier or the Sokoto gap-filler should add it.
Counterparts: sultanate-of-agadez (no dossier), songhai-empire, sokoto-caliphate (exist). Gazetteer: Leka, Surame, Argungu (places).
